checked_scope: Two-agent construction, zero-marginal removals and matroid-rank representation
checks: Binary increments restrict a violating transfer to costs {r-1,r} and {s,s+1}. If removal lowers r, integrality forces s<=r-2; otherwise a rising low cost lowers -s, and unchanged costs lower the higher-bundle size. Every case strictly decreases (r,-s,h).

There are at most (m+1)^3 potential triples and O(m) removal queries per move. Cut-and-choose gives complete two-agent EFX: cutter accepts either bundle and chooser is envy-free by monotonicity, including zero-removal-marginal chores.

For binary submodular costs, c(S)=|S| sets are hereditary and satisfy augmentation by diminishing zero marginals. Greedy retained independent subsets have size c(S), proving the matroid-rank representation without treating redundancy as additive free items.
